Amazon.Family owns: nothing stored — the parent row carries zero populated fields; “non-varying attributes” are replicated on every child.
Amazon.Member owns: everything: title, description, bullets, images, price (on the seller-side listing), identifiers.
Amazon.The policed rule: “Terms like ‘item type keyword’, ‘model name’, ‘style’ and ‘brand’ are key non-varying attributes for which all child ASINs must have the same values. Child ASINs with different non-varying attribute values cannot be grouped.”
Amazon.One product, two families?: no — “a single, non-sellable parent product”; feed error 8032 on re-parenting.
Amazon.Example: ● parent + 3 children byte-identical on title stem, description, bullet-point1, search-terms, main-image-url — on a defective flavour family (Clif Bar: flavor empty on all rows); the Size/Color families in Flat.File.Home.xls are clean

Shopify.Member owns: title (the variant title), media, selectedOptions, price, sku, barcode, inventoryItem. No description field on the variant.
Shopify.The policed rule: none needed — the field is absent.
Shopify.One product, two families?: no (by the shape of the key).

Google.Member owns: everything else (title, description, brand, gtin, price, link, image).
Google.The policed rule: “All variants of the same product must have the same item group title”, and it must differ from the member [title]; description/brand/gtin/category: not stated (U9, re-read 2026-09-21).
Google.Example: ● "itemGroupTitle": "cp0905 u3 flavor group" vs "title": "cp0905 u3 flavor - mango"

eBay.Family owns: InventoryItemGroup {title, description, imageUrls, aspects, variesBy} — title/description 0..1 optional in §1.4; on the Wayback route they “become the listing title and listing description”.
eBay.The policed rule: “the product.title and product.description values … must have the same values” — Wayback route only; not in #11045.
eBay.One product, two families?: no (by the shape of the key).
eBay.Example: ● Browse item v1|110590192388|410111412258: title: "Cotton T-Shirt 1786672804899" = itemGroupTitle; second member differs on Size = M only

Walmart.The policed rule: must: same variantGroupId · same variantAttributeNames · values for the same variant attributes · unique combination · exactly one primary. Content: a best practice only — “Keep product content consistent across all variants except for the attributes that vary.”
Walmart.One product, two families?: no — “An item can belong to only one variant group.”
Walmart.Example: ● both members carry "productName": "Colgate Crest Toothpaste" and differ on flavor only

Shopee.Family owns: the item — item_name, description (one of 32 item_list children), category, brand, attribute_list, images.
Shopee.The policed rule: none needed — the model has no such fields.

Tokopedia.Member owns: skus[]: sales attributes, price, inventory, identifier code, SKU image, sku_dimensions/sku_weight.
Tokopedia.Example: ● Create Product body: title/description required at depth 0; skus[].price, skus[].identifier_code

Square.The policed rule: none needed; images free-form on both levels.

Salesforce B2C.Member owns: anything it sets; unset values fall back.
Salesforce B2C.The policed rule: none — “If the variant does not define an own value, the value is retrieved by fallback from variation groups (sorted by their position) or the variation master.”
Salesforce B2C.One product, two families?: no — “you assign a variation group to only one base product.”
Salesforce B2C.Example: ◇ variant sets description, inherits name — no retrieved instance data (U9)

Akeneo.Family owns: the product model's common attributes — “the name, the collection, the description, the brand, etc.” — configurable per family variant.
Akeneo.Member owns: the level-2 attributes (sku, weight, size, ean in the vendor example).
Akeneo.The policed rule: structural: an attribute lives at exactly one level.

WooCommerce.Member owns: description (“Variation description”), sku, gtin, price, stock, image, the selected axis values.
WooCommerce.The policed rule: none — the storefront renders <div class="woocommerce-variation-description"> per selection and swaps the gallery.
WooCommerce.One product, two families?: no — post_parent; a non-product parent is reset to 0.
WooCommerce.Example: ● variation property table: description | string | Variation description.

commercetools.Example: ● Modular VariantProjection.description? = “Description of the parent Product” — a read-only projection

Magento.Family owns: the configurable parent row — but every product row has description and short_description.
Magento.Member owns: a full product row (simple product) — description included; whether a child's description ever renders on a configurable page is not stated (0 hits on Adobe's page, 2026-06-15).
